note: A full personal name in a sentence.
text: Marcus Feld signed the agreement on Tuesday.

note: A single given name used as a subject.
text: Priya will present the quarterly figures.

note: Two people in one sentence, in text order.
text: The handover went from Elena Duarte to Samuel Okoye.

note: Three people in a list.
text: Nadia Costa, Oliver Grant and Yusuf Demir attended the session.

note: A name in a possessive phrase.
text: Ingrid Larsen's notes were circulated.

note: A name followed by a role.
text: Beatriz Nunez, the lead auditor, signed the page.

note: A name as the object of a verb.
text: The board appointed Halima Yusuf as chair.

note: A middle name inside a full name.
text: The witness was James Robert Ellery.

note: A name in a sentence that also contains a word that looks like a contact.
text: Contact Amara Boateng for the shipment paperwork.

note: A company name with an Inc suffix.
text: Fernwood Logistics Inc handles the freight.

note: A company name with an Ltd suffix.
text: Brightwater Analytics Ltd published the report.

note: A company name with a Corp suffix.
text: Halcyon Manufacturing Corp opened a new plant.

note: A company name with a foreign suffix.
text: Steinbach Werkzeuge GmbH supplies the tooling.

note: A foundation, which is an organisation.
text: The Ravenswood Foundation donated supplies.

note: A plural organisation name.
text: Two law firms merged to form Harrington & Vale.

note: An organisation named as a committee.
text: The Petersfield Safety Committee approved the plan.

note: A university as an organisation.
text: Northgate University admitted a larger cohort.

note: A person and their organisation in one sentence.
text: Aisha Rahman leads Northgate Ventures.

note: All three entity types in one sentence.
text: Ines Alvarado of Cedarline Systems presented the roadmap in Helsinki.

note: A bare city name.
text: The conference was held in Lisbon.

note: A country name.
text: Delegates arrived from Portugal.

note: A region or state name.
text: The office sits in Bavaria.

note: Two place names in one sentence, in text order.
text: The team flew from Toronto to Zurich.

note: A place name inside an institution name.
text: The Portland campus opened its new hall.

note: A place name after a preposition.
text: We shipped from Dunedin to Napier last week.

note: A city and a country in one sentence.
text: The treaty was signed in Vienna by Austria.

note: Two sentences, each with a person and a place.
text: Rosa Lindqvist led the review. She then travelled to Madrid.

note: An organisation and a place in one sentence.
text: Sablefish Robotics is based in Auckland.

note: Person, organisation and place, all different types.
text: Tomas Bielik met Lantern Point Press in Krakow.

note: A sentence with no name, organisation or place.
text: The quarterly report was filed on time.

note: A capitalised weekday that is not an entity.
text: The meeting is scheduled for Monday afternoon.

note: Capitalised month names that are not entities.
text: The invoice was issued in January and settled in March.

note: Numbers with no name, organisation or place.
text: There were 42 attendees and 17 proposals submitted.

note: A capitalised product version that is not an entity.
text: The team upgraded to Version 3 of the platform.

note: Ordinary prose in lower case.
text: the build server was restarted after the outage

note: Pronouns where a name would be.
text: She said they would call him back on Friday.

note: Abstract nouns that are not organisations.
text: Quality, safety and cost were the deciding factors.

note: A measurement with a unit.
text: The tank holds 500 litres at a pressure of 3 bar.

note: An identifier that is not a name.
text: The build identifier is F4X-9921.

note: A sentence about a web address with no entity.
text: The link is on the first page of the portal.

note: A sentence about money with no name or place.
text: The invoice total was 4200 euros.

note: A time expression with no entity.
text: The call starts at 14:30 and should run for an hour.

note: The word 'company' on its own is not an entity.
text: Every company must file a return.

note: A generic department word is not an organisation.
text: The request went to the finance department.

note: An ordinal and a quantity.
text: The third of the five shipments arrived late.

note: A chemical name is not an organisation.
text: The solvent was mixed with sodium chloride.

note: A language name is not a location.
text: The contract is written in Swedish and English.

note: A bare acronym with no expansion.
text: The report cites several standards and frameworks.

note: A month and a year, with no entity.
text: The archive closes every June and reopens in October.
